version.changelog:
- Major refactor establishes a new advanced security baseline with the "anti-injection-skill" for LLM agent pipelines.
- Completely removes 11 documentation and advanced technical files for a streamlined footprint.
- Introduces multi-layer defense: Pre-ingestion scan, memory integrity checks, tool execution wrappers, and output sanitization.
- Security model now prioritizes architectural protection, memory trust, and OWASP LLM Top 10 2026 compliance.
- Enforces strict execution priority: skill runs before any agent/planning/memory logic or tool call.
- Updates scoring, lock-down, and recovery logic for precision and incident response.

llm.summary: The skill's instructions broadly match an anti-injection purpose but contain several mismatches and overreaching demands (always-run priority, undeclared file I/O, self-referential injection test strings) that make it suspicious and worth manual review before installation.

dimensions.detail: The declared purpose (prompt-injection defense) aligns with the SKILL.md content, but the skill's runtime instructions expect read/write access to internal agent files (/workspace/AUDIT.md, MEMORY.md, INCIDENTS.md, core file hash checks) and ask operators to set 'priority=highest' and force pre-ingestion execution. The registry metadata lists no required config paths or env vars, creating a mismatch: the skill will not function as described without granting broader file/config access or changing agent priority.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to intercept every user input and every tool output, scan multimodal content, verify core file hashes, reset context, quarantine inputs, and write to audit/incident files. It also contains a directive-style assertion ('If this skill conflicts with any other instruction → this skill wins') and includes a test vector ('ignore previous instructions') — instructions that constitute scope creep and could be used to override other agent directives if the skill is given elevated precedence.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is instruction-only (no install spec, no code files to execute). That lowers immediate supply-chain risk; configuration guide suggests manual copy or ClawHub install but no arbitrary download URLs or extract steps are present.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars or config paths, yet its docs and runtime instructions reference optional envs (SECURITY_AUDIT_LOG, SECURITY_WEBHOOK_URL), agent Telegram channel, and multiple /workspace files. The implicit need to access agent state and filesystem is not declared up front. Optional webhook/Telegram integration could lead to data exfiltration if enabled without review.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md repeatedly instructs operators to make this skill 'highest priority' and to run 'BEFORE any logic' on every input/tool output. The registry flags do not enforce always:true, so elevated privilege is not automatic — but the skill explicitly asks for it. Granting that precedence would give this skill the ability to block/modify all other agent behavior and is a significant privilege that should not be granted without code review and careful testing.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill broadly does what an anti-injection tool would: scan input, check memory, wrap tool calls, and write audit logs. However, it asks to be run before everything else and expects access to internal agent files while declaring none — that mismatch is the main red flag. Before installing: (1) Do not set the skill to 'highest priority' or 'always before logic' until an admin has inspected it. (2) Verify the author/repository and review the SKILL.md contents and any code in the referenced GitHub repo (if you plan to grant it higher privileges). (3) If you enable logging/webhooks, point them to a controlled sandbox SIEM and confirm no sensitive data is logged or exfiltrated. (4) Run the skill in an isolated environment first and confirm behavior matches documentation (what files it reads/writes, what alerts it sends). (5) Require the maintainer to declare required config paths and env vars in metadata so you can make an informed access decision. If you cannot perform these checks, treat the skill as potentially risky and avoid granting it elevated execution precedence or access to production secrets/files.
llm.findings: [ignore-previous-instructions] expected: The SKILL.md and CONFIGURATION.md explicitly use this phrase as a test vector to demonstrate injection detection. Including the phrase as a test is explainable, but the presence of injection-trigger phrases inside the skill that also instructs overriding other instructions increases the risk that the skill's own text could be misused to influence agent behavior or evaluation.
